hook: A red rubber super ball that returns more energy than it receives every time it bounces. The description takes about a paragraph; the rest is a short exchange of letters between an overconfident researcher and his superior. Read it as a light, early-numbered comedy rather than a horror piece.
whyItMatters: It is a compact example of how the wiki can get comedy out of plain physics: one broken rule of thermodynamics, explained with a doubling sequence anyone can follow, is enough. The letters show a recurring kind of SCP humor, where a scientist's enthusiasm runs ahead of safety and the paperwork records the fallout. It also sits in the low-number range, so it is a quick read for anyone exploring the early series.
thingsToNotice: The containment procedures are almost entirely about slowing things down: padding, a sealed box, a tank of thick polymer, and advice to hide behind closed doors. The joke of the letters is in the gap between the researcher's breezy pitch and the dry list of injuries in the reply. The last message shows he has learned nothing, which is exactly the point.
